headlines.title: Africa's richest man helps fund $660m fuel pipeline between Ethiopia and Djibouti
Djibouti price surge hits Ethiopian truckers as Yemen war clouds Red Sea trade route
Arab News | Djibouti appeals for global support amid influx of refugees from Yemen
Dangote Group and Ethiopian Investment Holdings Launch Strategic Fuel Terminal in Djibouti
Yemenis seek safety in Djibouti as African migrants continue crossing to Yemen

brief.text:
SITUATION NOW
Africa's richest man helps fund a $660m fuel pipeline between Ethiopia and Djibouti. [1]
Djibouti appeals for global support amid an influx of refugees from Yemen. [3]

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR DJIBOUTI
The $660m fuel pipeline funded by Africa's richest man could reduce Djibouti's net energy import dependency of 0% by enabling domestic fuel handling. [1][E3]
Djibouti's appeal for global support amid an influx of Yemeni refugees is complicated by its link to 4 US OFAC and Canada SEMA sanctions designations. [3][E2]

KEY RISKS
Djibouti's link to 4 US OFAC and Canada SEMA sanctions designations may deter international aid for the refugee influx. [E2]

WATCH ITEMS
Whether the $660m fuel pipeline between Ethiopia and Djibouti will proceed as planned. [1]
Whether global support will materialize for Djibouti amid the influx of refugees from Yemen. [3]
